card.name: Setup of two-way drug interaction phrases
card.fires_on: Small words like "of", "Drug" or "Conversely," right where a drug-interaction heading or sentence is about to name the other direction (drug A on drug B, then the reverse).

modes.label: Interaction headings
modes.description: The word "of", "Effect", "Effects" or "Potential" in section headings about one drug's effect on another.
modes.example: 7.2<< Effects>> of Other Drugs on HEPCLUDEX

modes.label: Table column headings
modes.description: The word "Drug" ending the phrase "Concomitant Drug" in interaction table headers.
modes.example: Effect on Concentration of Darunavir Or Concomitant<< Drug>> Clinical Comment HIV-1-Antiv

modes.label: Reversal wording
modes.description: Words that flip the direction of an order or relation, such as "Conversely," or "not the".
modes.example: Conversely<<,>> at least 5 weeks should be allowed

card.writes: It suppresses words like reciprocal, vice, mutual and 'the other way round', so it seems to mark the reversed direction as not yet stated.
card.plain: It fires on little words in drug-interaction headings and reversal phrases, where the text is about to say which drug acts on which.
